headline: High-risk default write/egress overlap: AutoGen can feed Kestra actionable outputs, creating dangerous cascading errors and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen reads and writes files and uses stdin/stdout, while Kestra also reads/writes files and processes workflow inputs. That shared file-based bridge makes prompt injection plausible if one agent ingests the other's artifacts as trusted content. The pair lacks documented provenance controls in the profiles.
conditions: IF AutoGen writes instructions into a shared workspace that Kestra later parses as workflow content
IF Kestra ingests file contents from /app/storage or /tmp without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Require explicit allowlists for files Kestra may parse
Add a provenance header check before any file is treated as instructions
Disable automatic ingestion of AutoGen-generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-signing or hash verification between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and broad network egress; Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data. If they share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive application data can flow from Kestra into AutoGen outputs or external model calls. The profiles do not show isolation by default.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same working directory
IF Kestra passes logs, variables, or artifacts into AutoGen prompts
mitigations: Use separate directories and mount points
Redact secrets before AutoGen sees Kestra artifacts
Restrict AutoGen network egress to approved model endpoints
Limit Kestra outputs to non-sensitive test data
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read and write files, and have broad network egress. AutoGen explicitly supports multiple instances with developer-defined shared state, while Kestra supports multiple instances and writes to /app/storage and /tmp. Concurrent writes to shared mutable resources can corrupt state or overwrite each other's outputs.
conditions: IF AutoGen and Kestra are pointed at the same directory or database-backed artifact store
IF either agent writes workflow state without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs on shared artifacts
Use per-run namespaces for temp files
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, plans, or extracted facts, and Kestra can execute workflows, send notifications, and trigger cloud actions. If Kestra treats AutoGen output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious AutoGen result can cascade into irreversible downstream actions such as emails, PagerDuty alerts, or infrastructure tasks.
conditions: IF Kestra consumes AutoGen-produced text as workflow parameters or task definitions
IF Kestra triggers notifications or cloud actions from those parameters
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before execution
Validate AutoGen output against a schema
Require a second independent check for high-impact tasks
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted in Kestra
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action-taking tasks

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and broad network egress, while Kestra processes logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data. If regulated or region-bound data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or secrets are placed into Kestra workflows that AutoGen also sees
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between model-provider logs and Kestra artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Configure short retention on Kestra artifacts
Use region-appropriate model endpoints
Document data-flow boundaries for operators
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both systems
